hints: Model the volume first: the rectangular tank has $V=2h$.
The net volume rate is inflow minus outflow, so $dV/dt=1-0.2\sqrt h$.
Combine this with $dV/dt=2\,dh/dt$, invert to obtain $dt/dh$, and integrate from $h=0$ to $h=4$.
walkthrough:
Relate the volume of water $V$ in the tank to the depth $h$:
Since the tank has vertical sides and a constant base area of $2\,\text{m}^2$, the volume at depth $h$ is:
$$V = 2h$$

Differentiate with respect to time $t$ to find the rate of change of volume:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t}$$

Set up the net rate of volume change using $\text{rate of inflow} - \text{rate of outflow}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = 1 - 0.2\sqrt{h}$$

Express $0.2$ as a fraction, $0.2 = \dfrac{1}{5}$, and combine the right-hand side over a common denominator:
$$2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = 1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{h}}{5} = \dfrac{5 - \sqrt{h}}{5}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{5 - \sqrt{h}}{10}$$

Invert to obtain an expression for $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}h}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}h} = \dfrac{10}{5 - \sqrt{h}}$$

Separate variables and integrate from $t = 0$ (depth $h = 0$) to $t = T$ (depth $h = 4$):
$$\int_0^T \mathrm{d}t = \int_0^4 \dfrac{10}{5 - \sqrt{h}}\,\mathrm{d}h$$
$$T = \int_0^4 \dfrac{10}{5 - \sqrt{h}}\,\mathrm{d}h$$

hints: Transform the integral from part (i) using the prescribed substitution $u=5-\sqrt h$.
Convert the bounds: $h=0$ gives $u=5$, while $h=4$ gives $u=3$; reverse them to remove the minus sign.
Simplify the integrand into a constant plus a multiple of $1/u$, integrate, and evaluate at $u=3$ and $u=5$.
walkthrough:
Use the given substitution $u = 5 - \sqrt{h}$ to express $h$ and $\mathrm{d}h$ in terms of $u$:
$$\sqrt{h} = 5 - u \implies h = (5 - u)^2 = 25 - 10u + u^2$$
$$\mathrm{d}h = 2(5 - u)(-1)\,\mathrm{d}u = -2(5 - u)\,\mathrm{d}u = 2(u - 5)\,\mathrm{d}u$$
(Or equivalently, $\mathrm{d}u = -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{h}}\,\mathrm{d}h \implies \mathrm{d}h = -2\sqrt{h}\,\mathrm{d}u = -2(5 - u)\,\mathrm{d}u$)

Determine the new limits of integration:
- When $h = 0$: $u = 5 - \sqrt{0} = 5$
- When $h = 4$: $u = 5 - \sqrt{4} = 5 - 2 = 3$

Substitute into the integral for $T$:
$$T = \int_5^3 \dfrac{10}{u}\big(-2(5 - u)\big)\,\mathrm{d}u$$

Use the negative sign to invert the limits from $\int_5^3$ to $\int_3^5$ and expand the integrand:
$$T = \int_3^5 \dfrac{20(5 - u)}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u = \int_3^5 \left(\dfrac{100}{u} - 20\right)\,\mathrm{d}u$$

Integrate each term with respect to $u$:
$$\int \left(\dfrac{100}{u} - 20\right)\,\mathrm{d}u = 100\ln u - 20u$$

Evaluate the definite integral between limits $u = 3$ and $u = 5$:
$$T = \Big[100\ln u - 20u\Big]_3^5 = \big(100\ln 5 - 20(5)\big) - \big(100\ln 3 - 20(3)\big)$$
$$T = (100\ln 5 - 100) - (100\ln 3 - 60) = 100(\ln 5 - \ln 3) - 100 + 60$$
$$T = 100\ln\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) - 40$$

Compute the decimal value:
$$\dfrac{5}{3} \approx 1.6666667$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) \approx 0.5108256$$
$$100\ln\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) \approx 51.08256$$
$$T \approx 51.08256 - 40 = 11.08256 \approx 11.1$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 11.1$ hours.
